term: What is a vertex in 3D graphics?
definition: A point in 3D space defined by X, Y, Z coordinates. Vertices are the building blocks of all 3D geometry.

term: What is a mesh?
definition: A collection of vertices, edges, and faces (polygons) that together define the shape of a 3D object.

term: What does PBR stand for in materials?
definition: Physically Based Rendering — a shading model that simulates how light interacts with surfaces using real-world material properties (albedo, roughness, metalness, normals).

term: What is UV mapping?
definition: The process of projecting a 2D texture image onto a 3D surface. U and V are the 2D coordinates (like X and Y, but for texture space).

term: What are the three main light types in 3D?
definition: Directional (like the sun, parallel rays), Point (like a bulb, emits in all directions), and Spot (like a flashlight, cone-shaped). Ambient light adds a flat base brightness.

term: What is a normal map?
definition: A texture that stores surface direction data (normals) to simulate fine surface detail (bumps, scratches) without adding real geometry.

term: What file format is known as the 'JPEG of 3D'?
definition: GLB / GLTF — the GL Transmission Format. It bundles geometry, materials, textures, and animations into a single optimized binary file ideal for the web.

term: What is Three.js?
definition: A JavaScript library that wraps WebGL, providing a higher-level API for creating 3D scenes in the browser without writing raw GPU shader code.

term: What is React Three Fiber (R3F)?
definition: A React renderer for Three.js. It lets you build Three.js scenes declaratively with JSX components like <mesh>, <boxGeometry>, and <Canvas>.

term: What is Spline?
definition: A no-code, browser-based 3D design tool that lets you create interactive 3D scenes and export them as embeddable web components — no coding required.

term: What is Blender used for in a web 3D workflow?
definition: Blender is a free open-source 3D modeling, rigging, and animation suite. In web workflows it's used to clean up AI-generated meshes, fix UV maps, and export optimized GLB files.

term: What is Meshy.ai?
definition: An AI tool that generates 3D models from text prompts or images. It outputs GLB/OBJ files with textures, ready to load in Three.js.

term: What is Tripo3D?
definition: A fast AI 3D generation tool that converts text or image prompts into 3D models in seconds, optimized for speed and polygon quality.

term: What output formats do AI 3D tools typically produce?
definition: GLB (binary GLTF), OBJ (geometry + MTL material file), and FBX (common for animation rigs). GLB is preferred for the web.

term: What is retopology?
definition: The process of recreating a 3D model's surface with cleaner, more optimized geometry. AI-generated meshes often need retopology to reduce polygon count and fix mesh flow.

term: Name a good text-to-3D AI prompt strategy.
definition: Be specific about shape, material, and scale: 'a low-poly ceramic coffee mug, blue glaze, 4 inches tall, smooth surface' outperforms 'a mug'.

term: What are the three essentials of every Three.js scene?
definition: A Scene (container for objects), a Camera (defines the viewpoint), and a Renderer (draws the scene to a canvas element using WebGL).

term: What is the Three.js animation loop pattern?
definition: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); renderer.render(scene, camera); } animate(); — calls itself recursively via requestAnimationFrame, targeting 60fps.

term: What is the difference between MeshBasicMaterial and MeshStandardMaterial?
definition: MeshBasicMaterial ignores lighting and always renders at full color. MeshStandardMaterial uses PBR and responds to scene lights, producing realistic shading.

term: How do you load a GLB model in Three.js?
definition: Use GLTFLoader from three/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js: loader.load('model.glb', (gltf) => { scene.add(gltf.scene); })

term: What is OrbitControls?
definition: A Three.js helper that adds mouse-driven camera orbiting, panning, and zooming around a target point. Import from three/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js.

term: What is the <Canvas> component in React Three Fiber?
definition: The root component that creates a Three.js renderer and scene, attaches to a DOM canvas element, and provides the R3F rendering context for all child components.

term: What does the useFrame hook do in R3F?
definition: Runs a callback every frame (inside the render loop), receiving the state and delta time. Used for animations: mesh.current.rotation.y += delta

term: What is @react-three/drei?
definition: A helper library for React Three Fiber that provides ready-made components like <OrbitControls>, <Environment>, <Html>, <Text>, and hooks like useGLTF.

term: How does useGLTF differ from GLTFLoader?
definition: useGLTF (from @react-three/drei) is a React hook that loads a GLB with Suspense support and caches the result. It's declarative and works with React's rendering model.

term: What is React Suspense used for in R3F?
definition: To handle async loading of 3D assets. Wrap components in <Suspense fallback={<LoadingUI />}> so the scene renders a placeholder while models/textures load.

term: What makes Spline suitable for non-coders?
definition: A drag-and-drop editor with a built-in physics engine, interaction system, and one-click export to embed code — no Three.js or shader knowledge needed.

term: How do you embed a Spline scene in a webpage?
definition: Use the <spline-viewer> web component: <script type='module' src='https://unpkg.com/@splinetool/viewer@latest/build/spline-viewer.js'></script> then <spline-viewer url='...'></spline-viewer>

term: What is @splinetool/react-spline?
definition: The official React package for Spline. Install with npm, then: import Spline from '@splinetool/react-spline'; <Spline scene='...' />

term: What polygon budget should you target for a Spline web scene?
definition: Under 50k triangles total for good performance. Use Spline's built-in simplify tool and keep textures at 1024x1024 or smaller for mobile-friendly load times.

term: What is GLTFLoader's bounding box trick used for?
definition: After loading a model, compute its bounding box, find the center, and reposition the model to center it at the origin — ensures it appears centered regardless of export origin.

term: What CSS property makes a Three.js canvas fill its parent?
definition: Set width: 100%; height: 100%; on the canvas, and position: relative; with a defined height on the container. Use renderer.setSize(container.offsetWidth, container.offsetHeight).

term: How do you add a subtle float animation to a 3D object?
definition: In the animation loop: object.position.y = Math.sin(clock.getElapsedTime() * 0.8) * 0.1; — this oscillates the Y position using a sine wave.

term: What is a common mobile fallback for heavy 3D hero sections?
definition: Detect touch/mobile with (window.matchMedia('(hover: none)').matches), then either show a static image, reduce polygon count, or disable the canvas entirely on very slow devices.

term: What is NeRF?
definition: Neural Radiance Field — an AI technique that reconstructs a 3D scene from 2D photos by training a neural network to predict volume density and color from any viewpoint.

term: What is photogrammetry?
definition: A technique that reconstructs 3D geometry from overlapping photos by finding matching feature points and computing depth. Apps like Polycam use it for mobile 3D capture.

term: What is Luma AI used for?
definition: Capturing NeRF-based 3D scenes from video using a mobile device. The output can be exported as a GLTF/GLB for use in web projects.

term: What is DRACOLoader and when should you use it?
definition: A Three.js loader extension that decompresses Draco-compressed GLB files. Use it whenever your GLB was exported with Draco compression to reduce download size by 80-90%.

term: What is an albedo map?
definition: The base color texture of a surface — what it would look like under pure white, flat light with no shadows. Also called a diffuse map.

term: What is a roughness map?
definition: A grayscale texture where white = rough (diffuse reflections) and black = smooth (mirror-like reflections). Controls the sharpness of light reflections.

term: Why must albedo textures use SRGBColorSpace in Three.js?
definition: Albedo textures are authored in gamma (sRGB) color space by artists. Three.js defaults to linear space, so setting SRGBColorSpace corrects the color and prevents washed-out appearance.

term: What is Polyhaven?
definition: A free online library of CC0 (public domain) PBR textures, HDR environment maps, and 3D models. Everything is free for commercial use, no attribution required.

term: What is an AO (Ambient Occlusion) map?
definition: A grayscale texture that darkens crevices and contact areas where indirect light is blocked. Applied to a second UV channel in Three.js via material.aoMap and geometry.setAttribute('uv2', ...).

term: What is a skeletal animation rig?
definition: A hierarchy of bones (an armature) that deform a mesh's vertices. Each vertex is 'weighted' to one or more bones, so moving a bone moves the connected mesh geometry.

term: What is Mixamo used for?
definition: Adobe's free service that auto-rigs a humanoid character (uploads a GLB/FBX → AI detects the skeleton) and provides a library of thousands of pre-made animations to download.

term: What is AnimationMixer in Three.js?
definition: The object that manages and plays animation clips on a 3D model. Create it with new THREE.AnimationMixer(model), then get actions with mixer.clipAction(clip) and call action.play().

term: Why do you call mixer.update(delta) in the animation loop?
definition: The AnimationMixer needs to advance its internal clock each frame. delta is the elapsed time since the last frame (from clock.getDelta()), ensuring animations play at the correct speed.

term: What is animation blending?
definition: Smoothly transitioning between two animation clips by fading one out and another in. Use action.crossFadeTo(nextAction, 0.5) in Three.js for a 0.5-second blend.

term: What is scroll-driven 3D?
definition: A technique where 3D scene properties (camera position, object rotation, material opacity) change in response to the page scroll position, creating cinematic parallax experiences.

term: How do you link scroll position to a Three.js camera?
definition: Listen to window.addEventListener('scroll', ...), compute scrollPercent = scrollY / (document.body.scrollHeight - window.innerHeight), then lerp camera.position along a path.

term: What is GSAP ScrollTrigger?
definition: A GreenSock plugin that synchronizes GSAP animations to scroll position. In R3F, use @gsap/react with useGSAP to animate Three.js object properties on scroll.

term: What does CSS position: sticky do for a 3D canvas?
definition: Keeps the canvas fixed in the viewport while the page content scrolls beneath it — a common pattern for Apple-style scroll experiences where 3D reacts to scroll but stays on screen.

term: What is a 3D product configurator?
definition: An interactive 3D viewer where users can change product attributes (color, material, finish) in real time. The 3D model updates instantly without reloading.

term: What is @google/model-viewer?
definition: A web component from Google that renders a GLB model with built-in OrbitControls, AR mode, and lazy loading. Add it with a script tag — no Three.js code required.

term: How do you switch materials at runtime in R3F?
definition: Use useState for the selected variant, then pass it to the material: <meshStandardMaterial color={selectedColor} />. React re-renders update the material automatically.

term: What is an environment map in 3D rendering?
definition: A 360° HDR image that wraps around the scene, reflecting off glossy surfaces. In R3F use <Environment preset='studio' /> from drei to instantly add realistic reflections.

term: What is the most effective prompt pattern for Three.js code generation?
definition: Be specific about the result: 'Write a self-contained Three.js r160 module that renders a spinning torus knot with MeshNormalMaterial, OrbitControls, and a black background. Use import maps for dependencies.'

term: Why might AI generate outdated Three.js code?
definition: Three.js has breaking changes between versions (e.g., r152 vs r168 changed color spaces, geometry attributes, and loader paths). Always specify the version and verify against the official changelog.

term: How can you use AI to write GLSL shaders?
definition: Describe the visual effect in plain English: 'Write a Three.js ShaderMaterial fragment shader that creates a pulsing gradient from teal to purple, animated with a u_time uniform.'

term: What is a good AI workflow for debugging Three.js errors?
definition: Paste the full error + the relevant code snippet + the Three.js version. Ask: 'This Three.js r168 scene gives this error. What changed in recent versions that could cause this?'

term: What R3F hook loads a GLB asynchronously with caching?
definition: useGLTF from @react-three/drei: const { scene } = useGLTF('/model.glb'). Works with React Suspense — the component suspends until the model is loaded.

term: What is the <Environment> component from drei?
definition: Adds IBL (Image-Based Lighting) to an R3F scene using a preset HDR environment. <Environment preset='studio' /> applies global reflections and ambient lighting instantly.

term: What Vite command creates a React project?
definition: npm create vite@latest my-project -- --template react, then cd my-project && npm install && npm install three @react-three/fiber @react-three/drei

term: What is a game loop?
definition: A continuous cycle that runs every frame: 1) Read input, 2) Update game state, 3) Render the scene. In Three.js this maps to requestAnimationFrame calling an animate() function.

term: How do you handle keyboard input in a Three.js game?
definition: Track key states in an object: const keys = {}; addEventListener('keydown', e => keys[e.code] = true); addEventListener('keyup', e => keys[e.code] = false). Check keys in the game loop.

term: What is Rapier.js?
definition: A high-performance physics engine for the web (@dimforge/rapier3d-compat). It handles rigid body dynamics, collision detection, joints, and character controllers — pairs well with Three.js.

term: What is THREE.Clock used for in games?
definition: It tracks real elapsed time. clock.getDelta() returns seconds since the last call, used to make movement frame-rate independent: position += speed * delta instead of a fixed amount.

term: What is AABB collision detection?
definition: Axis-Aligned Bounding Box — the simplest collision check. Creates box-shaped hitboxes aligned to world axes. Three.js Box3 supports this with box.intersectsBox(otherBox).

term: What is LOD in game development?
definition: Level of Detail — swapping high-polygon models for lower-polygon versions as the camera moves away. Three.js has a built-in LOD object: scene.add(new THREE.LOD()).

term: What is a reasonable polygon budget for a web game object on mobile?
definition: ~5,000 triangles per major character/object on mobile, ~50,000 on desktop. Keep total scene polygons under 300k for smooth 60fps on mid-range devices.

term: What is Kenney.nl?
definition: A website by Kenney Vleugels offering thousands of free CC0 2D and 3D game assets (characters, environments, UI) — great for prototyping without creating assets from scratch.

term: What AI tool auto-rigs a custom 3D character for game animation?
definition: Mixamo (Adobe) automatically detects the skeleton of an uploaded humanoid mesh and generates a rig, plus hundreds of downloadable animation clips in FBX or GLB format.

term: What are the two shader stages in WebGL?
definition: Vertex shader (runs once per vertex, outputs gl_Position to place it in screen space) and Fragment shader (runs once per visible pixel/fragment, outputs the final color).

term: What is a GLSL uniform?
definition: A variable passed from JavaScript to a GLSL shader that stays constant across all vertices/fragments in a single draw call. Used for time, colors, resolution, mouse position, etc.

term: How do you animate a shader with time in Three.js?
definition: Add a uniforms object: { u_time: { value: 0.0 } }, create a ShaderMaterial with it, then update uniforms.u_time.value = clock.getElapsedTime() in the animation loop.

term: What GLSL function produces a repeating wave pattern?
definition: sin() — for example: float wave = sin(position.x * 5.0 + u_time * 2.0); produces a wave that moves over time. Multiply by an amplitude to control wave height.

term: What is shaderMaterial from @react-three/drei?
definition: A factory function that creates a reusable Three.js ShaderMaterial as a typed R3F component: const WaveMaterial = shaderMaterial({ u_time: 0 }, vertexShader, fragmentShader)

term: What is a draw call?
definition: One instruction from CPU to GPU to render a batch of geometry. Minimizing draw calls is the #1 performance optimization — each separate mesh is typically one draw call.

term: What is InstancedMesh?
definition: A Three.js class that renders thousands of identical objects in a single draw call using instancing. Each instance has its own transform matrix, but shares geometry and material.

term: What is Draco compression?
definition: An open-source geometry compression algorithm developed by Google. It reduces GLB geometry data by 80-95%, dramatically cutting download sizes. Enable during Blender export or with gltf-transform.

term: What is KTX2 texture compression?
definition: A GPU-native texture format that stays compressed in GPU memory (unlike PNG/JPEG which decompress on upload). Reduces GPU memory usage by 4-8x. Use Basis Universal for cross-platform support.

term: What is frustum culling?
definition: Automatically skipping rendering of objects outside the camera's view frustum. Three.js does this by default. Ensure mesh.frustumCulled = true (the default) is not accidentally disabled.

term: What are Blender's two main work modes for 3D objects?
definition: Object Mode (manipulate whole objects: move, scale, rotate) and Edit Mode (edit vertices, edges, faces of individual geometry). Press Tab to toggle between them.

term: What is the Y-up vs Z-up problem in Blender exports?
definition: Blender uses Z-up by default; GLTF/Three.js uses Y-up. The Blender GLTF exporter handles this automatically — but AI-generated models from other tools may arrive rotated 90°, requiring a manual rotation fix.

term: What gltf-transform command optimizes a GLB file?
definition: npx gltf-transform optimize input.glb output.glb --draco applies Draco compression, texture resizing, and mesh simplification in one command. Install: npm install -g @gltf-transform/cli

term: What Blender export settings matter most for web?
definition: ✓ Apply Transforms, ✓ Draco mesh compression, ✓ Include materials and textures, ✗ No cameras/lights unless needed. Keep 'Format' as glTF Binary (.glb) for a single file.

term: What is UV unwrapping in Blender?
definition: The process of cutting a 3D mesh and flattening it to a 2D plane so textures can be applied. Without proper UV unwrapping, textures will stretch or tile incorrectly on the mesh.

term: When should you use Meshy vs Blender for a 3D asset?
definition: Meshy: when you need an asset quickly and don't need precision control. Blender: when topology, exact dimensions, or animation rigs matter. Often best to start with Meshy and refine in Blender.

term: What is the typical AI-assisted 3D web pipeline order?
definition: 1) Text prompt → Meshy/Tripo3D, 2) Download GLB, 3) Optional Blender cleanup, 4) gltf-transform optimize, 5) AI textures/Mixamo animation, 6) Three.js/R3F rendering, 7) Deploy

term: When should you use Spline instead of Three.js?
definition: Use Spline for marketing sites, hero sections, and non-interactive showcases where you want fast iteration without code. Use Three.js/R3F when you need custom logic, game mechanics, or dynamic data.

term: What is the main advantage of React Three Fiber over vanilla Three.js?
definition: Declarative JSX syntax, React's component model (reusability, hooks, context), and ecosystem integration (state management, routing). Vanilla Three.js is faster for low-level control and non-React projects.

term: What deployment platform is simplest for a Three.js project?
definition: GitHub Pages (free, static hosting, automated via Actions) or Vercel (free tier, automatic deploys from git push, supports environment variables). Both work for static HTML/JS builds.

term: What is the difference between a 3D portfolio site and a 3D product configurator?
definition: A portfolio site uses 3D for visual storytelling and aesthetics (hero sections, scroll effects). A configurator is an interactive tool where users change product attributes and see 3D updates in real time.

term: What is Shadertoy?
definition: A browser-based GLSL shader playground and community. You can write, run, and share WebGL shaders directly in the browser — great for experimenting with visual effects after completing this course.

term: What is Three.js Journey?
definition: A popular paid video course by Bruno Simon that teaches Three.js in depth — widely regarded as the best comprehensive Three.js learning resource for those wanting to go deeper after basics.

term: What does the <primitive> component do in R3F?
definition: Renders any Three.js object directly in the JSX tree: <primitive object={gltf.scene} />. Used when you need to insert a pre-built Three.js object (like a loaded GLTF scene) into R3F.

term: What is the GLTF scene graph structure?
definition: A GLTF file contains a tree of nodes (objects), each with a transform, mesh, and optional animation/skin data. The root is gltf.scene in Three.js, which you add to the Three.js Scene.
